documents.title: 14 NYCRR § 686.6 - Administration (policy/procedure manual content required of each community residence)
documents.form_number: None. No OPWDD policy checklist form was found; 14 NYCRR 686.6 is the section that lists the required written policies.
documents.issuer: NYS Office for People With Developmental Disabilities (OPWDD), 14 NYCRR Part 686 (text via Cornell LII)
documents.version: Amended NYS Register 9/21/2016 (eff. 9/21/2016); the current LII text shows no later amendment
documents.how_used: Primary source for the policy and procedure manual. Section 686.6(a)(2) says each community residence must develop and implement policies/procedures addressing the listed topics 'at a minimum'. Section 686.6(b)(3) lists the manual contents OPWDD surveys for.

documents.title: 14 NYCRR § 686.8 - Program for supportive community residences (supportive CR/IRA policy additions)
documents.version: Justia text current through NYS Register 47, No. 25 (June 25, 2025)
documents.how_used: Applies only to supportive community residences. It adds referral/intake/admission and discharge-criteria policies, and extra items for the manual required by 686.6(a)(2).

required_items.text: Each community residence shall develop and implement policies/procedures which address, at a minimum:
Admission, including at least:

The process to determine an applicant's need for service, the ability of the facility to meet the ongoing needs of the individual, and consideration of the relevance of the family intactness and geographic proximity of the family.
The requirement that staff and the applicant participate in the above process, including the final determination as to the applicant's admission.
The procedures for obtaining admission.
The applicant criteria, in functional terms for admission.

The requirement that, to determine that an applicant meets the criteria prior to admission, it is necessary that the following information be reviewed: (1) the results of a medical/physical examination conducted within 90 days prior to the review; and (2) an assessment or assessments of an applicant's strengths, needs, interests and living skills completed within 90 days prior to the review.
The requirement that, no person shall be admitted over his or her objection, except by a court order.

The requirement that no person shall be excluded from a residence on the basis of race, religion, color, age, gender, national origin, or inability to pay for services. This shall not preclude a facility from establishing specific admission criteria that limit the range of the age or level of disability of the individuals, or their gender when necessitated by the overall objective of the facility.

The requirement that each applicant, or parent, guardian or correspondent as available, is informed in writing prior to admission and as changes occur of any charges (see section 686.12) and the supplies and services provided by the facility (see section 686.13), unless the applicant is a capable adult and objects to such notification to others.
Discharge, including at least:
The criteria for discharge of individuals.

The requirement that, to avoid precipitous discharge, reasonable efforts are made on the part of the community residence to meet the needs of a person before a more restrictive placement is sought and/or discharge is contemplated, taking into consideration the needs of the other individuals in the facility and the facility's available resources.
The procedures for being discharged, including the procedures governing discharge of a person against the recommendations of the program planning team.
The requirement that no overt or covert physical or psychological pressure shall be applied to prevent a person who desires to leave from doing so.
The requirement that those responsible for program planning participate in designing plans and the coordination of services for a person in the process of being discharged from the residence.

Review and appeal procedures available to individuals and their parents, guardians, or correspondents, including but not limited to appeal of the plan of services and placement decisions, which are in conformance with the regulations of the commissioner.

Community involvement, providing direction to staff and individuals as to the type of activities that will promote and nurture the involvement of the community residence with the neighborhood and community.

The means whereby individuals, in accordance with their capability, contribute to the decisionmaking process relative to the day-to-day activities at the community residence, and individual/staff involvement in neighborhood/community activities.
Requirements for the administration of the following:
plans of services;
person's financial records;
confidentiality and protection of individuals' records;
coordination, collection, release and tracking of statistical information;
incidents and allegations of abuse; and
medication administration, the current certification status of community residence staff to administer medications, and the self-administration of medication training program for individuals.

Medical emergencies, other potential emergencies, evacuation procedures to meet the special needs of persons with developmental disabilities, and disasters; the necessary staff actions associated with these situations; and the means to familiarize staff with these policies and procedures.
Health and safety issues.
Personnel policies/procedures addressing at least:
the recruitment and hiring process; qualifications, education and skills required; job descriptions; description of duties and responsibilities; and job performance evaluations;

staff training programs which include at a minimum: (1) coordination of staff development and training that is consistent with individuals' and staff needs and agency/facility policies; (2) orientation procedures; (3) in-service training; and (4) the use of community training resources;
the means whereby matters of concern to staff can be made known without threat of job loss; and
the prohibition of discrimination in hiring and promotion based on race, religion, color, gender, national origin, age or disability.
The approval process for policies/procedures, which includes a description of the role of the governing body in this process.
The agency/facility policy/procedure manual is a public document and, as such, shall be available to individuals, parents, guardians, correspondents, staff and others.

A written policy/procedure manual(s) exists with contents addressing the following areas: (i) admission and discharge of individuals; (ii) administration of records; (iii) emergencies and disasters; (iv) health and safety issues; (v) personnel; (vi) review and appeal procedures for concerns of individuals and their correspondents; (vii) community involvement of staff and individuals; and (viii) individuals' involvement in community residence activities.

The agency/facility has written criteria for a residence manager which mandate that the person in the position has, at a minimum, been awarded a high school diploma or its equivalent and has at least one year of experience working with persons with developmental disabilities.

A facility receiving an operating certificate as an individualized residential alternative, shall develop a site specific written plan for protective oversight. The plan shall include provisions for ensuring:
The assessment of each person's need for the amount and type of supervision necessary including both staff and/or technology as appropriate to the person and circumstance.
The use of appropriately trained substitute personnel when the primary assigned personnel are unavailable.
The establishment of qualifications and training requirements of those responsible for supervision.
The establishment of a process whereby the person's continuing need for the originally recommended amount and type of protective oversight can be periodically reviewed, and modified as necessary.
Each facility in this class shall ensure the provision of, or provide as its minimum responsibility, protective oversight (see glossary) appropriate to the person's needs.

OPWDD shall verify that each individualized residential alternative has implemented a facility evacuation plan. OPWDD shall verify that staff and persons residing in the facility are trained and evaluated regarding their performance of said plan.

OPWDD shall verify that each person has a plan for protective oversight, based on an analysis of the person's need for same, and that such need has periodically, but at least annually, been reviewed, revised as appropriate, and integrated, as appropriate, with other services received.

OPWDD shall verify that persons living in the facility are receiving appropriate protective oversight in accordance with the following: (i) any parties with supervision responsibilities have received training appropriate to the protective oversight needs of the persons in the facility including, but not limited to, first aid; (ii) any parties with supervision responsibilities are aware of the specifics of each person's plan for protective oversight; and (iii) each person's plan for protective oversight is being implemented as specified in the person's individualized service plan.
The agency/facility shall develop policies/procedures governing referral, intake and admission. (Supportive community residences)

These policies and procedures shall specifically address how the agency/facility will assess and meet the applicant's need for supervision in the supportive community residence, and shall include criteria justifying admission as listed in paragraph (b)(1) of this section.

There shall be discharge criteria which: (i) describe the level of independent functioning that would appropriately permit a person to live independently; and identify those activities and experiences which would promote such increased independence; (ii) describe potential problem circumstances or degenerating person functioning level which might result in discharge to a more restrictive program; and (iii) preclude discharge except to a setting which can more appropriately meet the person's needs and such a setting is actually available at the time of projected discharge.

The policy and procedure manual, as required in section 686.6(a)(2) of this Part shall also incorporate: (i) the requirement that a trained person shall be available to make visitations to a person in a supportive community residence in the absence of the assigned case manager; (ii) the requirement that a person shall be informed of the persons to call in the event of an emergency or other unusual or unsettling circumstances; (iii) the requirement that all occupants of a supportive community residence shall be trained to evacuate the facility in emergency situations; and (iv) any other necessary information specific to the operation of a supportive community residence.

notes: No single OPWDD policy checklist or form was found, so the required items come from regulation sections that list required written policies. The IRA Operating Certificate Application (OMR 248, cited in your source list) could not be retrieved: the businessexpress.ny.gov page returned a permission error, and searches did not surface the form. If you can get OMR 248 from OPWDD, check it against this list. (1) The manual is the agency's policy/procedure manual under 686.6(a)(2). OPWDD's stated intent in 686.2(b) is that the policies reflect compliance with Part 686 and become part of the agency's/facility's manual(s). The manual is a public document, so it must be available to individuals, parents, guardians, correspondents, staff and others (686.6(a)(3)). (2) 686.16(a)(4) lists the Part 686 sections an IRA must meet and does not name 686.6 or 686.8. 686.6(a)(2) applies to 'each community residence', and 14 NYCRR 619.2 treats IRAs as a community residence type. I therefore treated 686.6 as applicable, but confirm this with the OPWDD regional office. 686.8 items apply only to supportive residences. (3) Some items cover residence-manager qualifications, in 686.6(b)(1), and the protective oversight plan for each person, in 686.16(b)(3)-(4). Those are written criteria or plans OPWDD verifies at survey, not manual topics. The 686.16(b)(2) fire-evacuation evaluation in each person's ISP and the 686.16(b)(5) fire-alarm audibility check are survey checks, not manual items, so they are not listed. (4) 686.6(a)(2)(vi) and the Part 633 sections in your regulation list (633.8 training, 633.15 personal funds, 633.17 medication, 633.22 criminal history checks) set the substance that those policies must follow. They do not themselves list required policy topics, so they are not itemized here. (5) The only sections of 686.6, 686.8 and 686.16 retrieved were the ones above. Justia's 686.8 and 686.16 text is current through June 2025, and Justia carries a disclaimer that it may not be the latest version. Verify against the official NYCRR (Department of State) text before submission. Organize the manual by the headings above, using the regulation's own numbering as a crosswalk, so reviewers can map each policy to its citation. Submission format and review procedures are 'prescribed by OPWDD' through the certification and application process under 14 NYCRR Part 619 (see 686.2(d)). Confirm the current submission method with the OPWDD regional office or Division of Quality Improvement.
